title: 17-Year-Old Held in Lucknow After Mother Killed in Family Dispute
excerpt: Police say a 17-year-old boy in Lucknow fatally attacked his 42-year-old mother with an iron wrench during an argument, then called his father and the police himself. The teenager is in custody and being questioned.
body:
• A 17-year-old boy has been detained in Lucknow after allegedly killing his 42-year-old mother with an iron wrench at the family residence on Thursday evening, according to police.
  • Police say the attack followed an argument over the teenager's gender identity; reporting differs on the precise nature of the dispute.
  • The teenager had been living separately from his parents for about four months and had asked to meet his mother that evening, police said.
  • After the incident, the teenager called his father and then contacted the police himself; a forensic team examined the scene and the investigation is ongoing.

A 17-year-old boy has been detained in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, after allegedly killing his 42-year-old mother with an iron wrench during an argument at the family residence on Thursday evening, police said. The woman died at the scene from head injuries.

According to police, the incident took place at around 9 pm on Thursday. The teenager, who had been living separately from his parents, had expressed a wish to meet his mother that evening, and his father called him home. Once there, the two got into an argument that escalated, and the boy allegedly struck his mother repeatedly with a wrench. Senior officers, including the local Deputy Commissioner of Police, reached the residence, and a forensic team examined the scene and collected evidence.

After the killing, the teenager called his father and informed him of what had happened, police said. He then contacted the police himself to report the incident. The teenager is now in custody and is being questioned as the investigation continues.

A household dispute over the teenager's identity

Police said the argument centred on the teenager's gender identity and long-running family disagreements over it. According to one report, the boy had sought gender-affirming surgery, which his mother opposed, advising medical and psychological intervention instead. Another report said the family had had long-standing disagreements over his sexuality, had decided to keep him at a distance over concerns about social stigma, and had rented him a separate room in Lucknow about four months ago, around 1.5 km from their home, providing monthly money for his expenses.

The teenager is the couple's only child, and his father works as a clothes trader, police said. According to police, the father told investigators that the boy had been experiencing mental-health difficulties and had received treatment at different hospitals. Police said they were examining this history as part of the investigation without drawing conclusions about its connection to the killing.

Media outlets have not named the minor, in keeping with Indian reporting norms that withhold the identities of children involved in criminal cases.

Legal process and what comes next

The teenager has been detained and is being questioned. Under India's Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, a child in conflict with the law is produced before a Juvenile Justice Board rather than tried as an adult by default; in cases involving alleged heinous offences by those aged 16 to 18, the board conducts a preliminary assessment before deciding whether the case is tried in children's court.

Police said investigators are examining the circumstances surrounding the killing, the family's disputes and the teenager's background as the probe continues. Further details, including any findings from the forensic examination and the post-mortem, are expected as the investigation progresses.

There is no direct diaspora angle to this case.
